links.note: Why writing in a diary was a strange experience for Anne - she had never written before and no one would be interested. It is about what a diary permits, which is 24169.
Why the diary felt strange to her - the frankness of writing for no reader but herself.
Whom Anne would allow to read her diary - a real friend, if she got one. 24167 is her writing because she has no such friend.
Only a real friend could read it - the absence of that friend is exactly why she writes.
What she named her diary - Kitty. 24168 is naming the diary so that writing becomes conversation.
The diary named Kitty - the listener Anne invents for herself.
Why Mr Keesing was annoyed with her - she was talkative. That is what the chatterbox essays punish.
Mr Keesing annoyed by her talking in class - the cause of the essay punishments.
The language the diary was originally written in - Dutch. A fact about the text and its author.
The diary's original language, Dutch - a fact about the source text.
When the diary was given to Anne - on her thirteenth birthday. A fact about the diary as a text.
The diary received as a thirteenth-birthday present - the origin of the text.
Why Anne thinks she was lonely - she had no real friends although she was surrounded by people. 24172 is precisely that loneliness beneath sociability.
Lonely despite having friends, because none truly understood her - 24172's subject.
What the class bet about - who would move up and who would be kept back. Ordinary school life going on, which is 24177.
The classroom betting over who would pass - school life continuing as usual.
How many siblings Anne had - one. Part of the family sketch she records.
Anne's one sibling - from the family sketch in her diary.
The name of Anne's sister - Margot, from the family sketch she writes down.
Margot, her sister - part of what Anne records about her family.
The only survivor of Anne's family - her father. That fact belongs to the wartime persecution 24176 describes.
Anne's father as the sole survivor - the outcome of the persecution the diary was written under.
The date on which she recorded the Keesing incident - 20 June 1942. The item tests the dating of entries, which is 24166.
The dated entry, 20 June 1942, in which the Keesing episode appears - 24166's day-by-day quality.
The subject she had to write on - 'Necessity of Talking'. One of the essays Mr Keesing set as punishment.
Grandma died in January 1942 - part of the family history Anne sets down in her diary.
Explaining 'teachers are the most unpredictable creatures' - Anne's playful tone about being punished, which is what 24170 names.
